prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live listings from here, but I can tell you the best options and how to pick the right place in Pleasanton so you get good tires and a solid installation.

Where to buy
- National/value options (good prices, broad inventory, reliable installs)
  - Costco Tire Center (great prices for members + good warranty/installation policies)
  - Discount Tire (large selection, competitive pricing, fast service)
  - Firestone Complete Auto Care / Goodyear / Pep Boys / NTB (frequent promotions and nationwide warranty)
- Performance or specialty tires
  - Tire Rack (often ships to a local recommended installer) or specialty local shops that focus on performance/aftermarket tires
- Local independent shops
  - Many independents in Pleasanton/Livermore/Dublin offer very personalized service and often competitive pricing — worth checking local reviews

Who does the best installation
- Chains above (Discount Tire, Costco, Firestone) are known for consistent, professional installations and good turnaround.
- Independent shops can be equal or better — especially if they advertise ASE-certified techs, road-force balancing, and have strong local reviews.
- “Best” depends on what matters to you: speed and warranty (Costco/Discount Tire), performance-oriented balancing and mounting (specialty shops/Tire Rack installers), or personalized long-term service (local independents).

How to choose the best installer (use this checklist when calling/booking)
- Ask if the techs are ASE-certified.
- Confirm what’s included in the installation price: mounting, balancing, valve stems, new rubber valve if relevant, TPMS reset/programming, disposal fee.
- Ask whether they use road-force balancers (recommended for high-performance or low-profile tires).
- Ask if wheel alignment is included or if they will check alignment after mount (alignment is often necessary after new tires).
- Ask about warranty handling and whether they register tires for you.
- Ask about torque specs and whether they re-torque lug nuts after 50–100 miles.
- Check turnaround time and if they accept appointments or do same-day installs.
- Read recent Yelp / Google reviews (look for comments about balance, vibration after install, and customer service).

What I recommend you do right now
1. Decide brand/priority: budget, all-season, performance, or off-road.  
2. Get quotes from 2–3 places (e.g., Costco if you’re a member, Discount Tire, and one well-rated local shop).  
3. Compare total price (tires + mounting + balancing + disposal + alignment if needed) and services as per the checklist above.  
4. Book an appointment and confirm re-torque policy and follow-up checks.

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code or cross streets in Pleasanton,
- vehicle make/model and tire size (or current tire size),
- budget and priorities (price vs. performance vs. warranty),
and I’ll give a short list of likely nearby places to call and specific questions to ask them.
